title: Prove the sharp Gram cost floor on all 23 physical C5s
body:
PR2782 left signed-half Gram decoding on the physical C5s unresolved. This proves that every finite Gram decoder on each of its 23 fixed C5 masks costs at least 20 under the inherited complete-plane tariff, and retains a cost-20 witness for each. Coefficients may be arbitrary rational, real or complex numbers; no coefficient menu or term-count limit is imposed.

Five forced four-port identity blocks each require four rank-one contributions. Exhaustively verified support inequalities let the complete-plane tariff pay for those contributions, giving the sharp bound. The package contains the written argument, all 736 finite geometric inequalities, source pins and positive witnesses. It also exhibits a concrete unequal-span asymmetric term where this proof's tariff inequality fails, making the scope boundary testable.

Validation:

- Registered standard-library CPython 3.12.15 replay passed: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c5-gram-rank-cover`.
- Nine controls pass on Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.4, including independently enumerated cycles and binary ranks, a rejected false cost-19 fit, signed undercharging, invalid normalization and source tampering. The wrong-mask and signed-tariff mutants are both detected.
- A separate Codex review independently recovered all 23 cycles and 736 inequalities with chordless-walk enumeration and dense binary elimination. This is AI review, not human or formal-kernel verification.
- Metadata/source-pin checks, `git diff --check`, and all nine publication-byte comparisons passed at `9d75ed2b5bc9bb8cb19f205724f978b02be732cb`.

This closes the fixed-instance signed-Gram question. It does not prove a global cost-224 floor, price arbitrary asymmetric decoders, supply a native word or improve kappa. No selected cold-chain replay was run. Selected results, frozen inputs and predecessor packages are unchanged.

Credit Tekalign/PR2782 for the physical instances, tariff and signed-half handoff; Arham Tahir/PR2879 for the related principal-block rank method; Sagar Thakrar/PR2484, Cinna Davis/PR1825, Adam Gall/PR1889, ctoth, Philippe Van Velzen and the retained selected-geometry lineage. Prepared by thakrarsagar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

Task: `coverage-law-change`, explicitly narrowed to this local obstruction under priority revision 6. Canonical main and fork were refreshed and synchronized; submission overlap covered 276 open PRs and 2050 Discussion records.
